rules: Roster: Add a standalone person only when a tracked decision establishes material authority, implementation, backing, or influence. Keep incidental mentions in event text and case participants in the legal record. Check structured links before pruning.

Representation: Record whose interests have a channel through access, fundraising, organizing, personnel, or financial ties. Identify the backer and recipient. Verify the kind of tie and distinguish announced, awarded, paid, and realized amounts.

Stance changes: Compare dated positions, audiences, decisions, and consequential acts. Record what the actor or backer stood to gain, what else changed, and any counterexample where the actor held a position at a cost.

Motives: Assess power, money, access, ideology, loyalty, status, audience, and survival on their own evidence. Record competing explanations and distinguish a documented benefit, an inferred motive, and evidence of influence.

Authority and scoring: Identify who decides, blocks, implements, and influences. Link each episode across relevant issues and count it once overall. Separate stages and score policy, access, formal authority, succession, and financial gain independently. Preserve legacy scores for comparison. Withhold credit when the relevant outcome or prior goal lacks support.
validation_checks: Check that each new person profile has a specific tracked role. Check that legal case participants render from case context and that retained subject links resolve.
Check that representation and financial flows are described separately, with dated evidence for claimed influence.
Check that repeated or bundled episodes have one overall scoring record and that each credited dimension has evidence.
Check that report and relationship claims reflect the reviewed evidence and label legacy conclusions.
workflow_review.next: Apply the workflow on the next intake and expand episode review before recalculating any overall ranking.
